[[measurement]]; [[means]] of assigning a [[magnitude]]. #: {{ux|en|Please rate your experience on a '''scale''' from 1 to 10.}} #: {{ux|en|The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the open-ended drawing, used to indicate measurement when the image has been [[magnified]] or [[reduced]]. #* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=ix|text=Even though precision can be carried to an extreme, the '''scales''' which now are drawn in (and usually connected to an appropriate figure by an arrow) will allow derivation of meaningful measurements.}} # {{senseid|en|series of musical notes}} ''The term migrated from tech/infrastructure (“can this system '''scale'''?”)'' to startups (“can this business '''scale'''?”)}} # {{sense|business: entrepreneurship, marketing and venture management, coordinate term to "grow"}} To increase revenues exponentially without proportional increases in costs. #* {{Q|en|Sarah Levinger|Post of "X" (formerly "Twitter")|year=May 12, 2025|quote=We started using the term '''“scaling”''' in place of “growing” around the late 1990s to early 2000s, primarily due to the rise of venture-backed startups in Silicon Valley. [...] VCs needed a way ''to describe businesses that could grow exponentially without adding proportional headcount or expense. So '''scalability''' became the holy grail''. The term migrated from tech/infrastructure (''“can this system '''scale'''?”'') to startups (''“can this business '''scale'''?”'') and now everyone from lifestyle brands to DTC businesses use it as a universal term for "make business go big." (By the mid-2010s, '''“scale”''' was in every pitch deck and founder tweet, even if what they really meant was: “We’re trying to 𝘨𝘳𝘰𝘸, but we want to sound smarter so we're using the term "'''scale'''".”) This change in language actually had a HUGE effect on the minds of the people who were operating businesses across the globe.}} #* {{Q|en|Alexandre Mathieu|Post on "Linked in"|year=2024|quote=Being able to move swiftly, try new things is critical in startups, so there shouldn't be friction upstream, but ''you need to make sure you have good process to purge things that don't '''scale''' with the rest''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[weigh]], [[measure]] or [[grade]] according to a scale or system. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Coriolanus|II|iii|passage='''Scaling''' his present bearing with his past.}} # {{lb|en|manufacturing|transitive}} To take measurements from (an {{w|engineering drawing}}), treating them as (or [[as if#Conjunction|as if]]) reliable [[dimension#Noun|dimensional]] instructions. #: {{ux|en|Every single drawing in the specification has a warning in its title block which reads, "Do not '''scale''' this drawing."}} =====Hyponyms===== {{col|en |scale back |scale down |scale out |scale up }} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|scale in|autoscale|blitzscale|downscale|prescale|rescale|scalability|scalable|scaler|unscale }} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|scaling ladder}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to change size of}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Dutch: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Māori: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|масштаби́ровать}} * Slovak: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to climb}} * Bulgarian: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Ido: * Japanese: * Latin: * Māori: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|взбира́ться|impf}} {{t+|ru|взобра́ться|pf}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to tolerate increases in throughput}} * Finnish: * Japanese: * Slovak: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to weigh}} * Finnish: * Slovak: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== [[File:Fish scales.jpg|thumb|Teleost '''scales''' ({{senseno|en|fish}})]] From {{inh|en|enm|scale}}, from {{der|en|fro|escale}}, from {{der|en|frk|-}} and/or {{der|en|goh|skala}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skalō}}.
